description: Auto Scaling groups must be configured to use a launch template rather than a launch configuration

decisionPoints.description: Which launch source, if any, the Auto Scaling group references: a launch configuration, a launch template directly, a launch template through a mixed instances policy, an existing EC2 instance, or nothing at all

Whether a launch source reference that is present actually identifies a target (a launch template identified by id or name, or a non-empty launch configuration name) or is present but carries no identifying value
Whether the launch source reference can be resolved at analysis time or is supplied by an input value only known at deployment

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references a launch configuration by name and declares no launch template reference and no mixed instances policy
requirements.rationale: The group's only instance configuration source is a launch configuration — the deprecated mechanism AWS no longer supports for new accounts or new instance types — so the deployed resource is exactly the state the rule prohibits.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether an Auto Scaling group whose sole instance-specification is LaunchConfigurationName (no LaunchTemplate, no MixedInstancesPolicy) ends up, in the service, using a launch configuration. It does: LaunchConfigurationName is the launch-configuration path and the service applies no launch-template default in its absence — an ASG must derive its instance spec from exactly one of launch configuration, launch template, or mixed instances policy, and here that one is the launch configuration. Searched AWS docs on launch configuration deprecation and the CloudFormation ASG property reference. The Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide "Create a launch configuration" and "Create Auto Scaling groups using launch configurations" pages both state: as of January 1, 2023 new EC2 instance types are no longer supported in launch configurations; accounts created on or after June 1, 2023 cannot create launch configurations via the console; and accounts created on or after October 1, 2024 cannot create new launch configurations by any method including CloudFormation. Both pages direct customers to migrate to launch templates. The AWS Compute Blog confirms launch templates are the successor and that no new EC2 features will be added to launch configurations. The CloudFormation reference confirms LaunchTemplate/LaunchTemplateSpecification is the separate, optional property that this configuration does not declare. Nothing about the omission is deployment-time-unknown: the resource unambiguously names a launch configuration, so the outcome is known at analysis time and breaches the rule.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references a launch template directly by launch template id together with a version, and declares no launch configuration
requirements.rationale: The group's instance configuration comes from a launch template specified by launch template ID plus version — a complete, valid LaunchTemplateSpecification — and no launch configuration is involved, which is exactly the state the rule requires.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup's LaunchTemplate/LaunchConfigurationName properties and for AWS guidance on launch templates vs launch configurations. The LaunchTemplateSpecification reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-launchtemplatespecification.html) states that a valid specification must give the ID or the name of the launch template (not both) plus the version — so "launch template id together with a version" is a fully valid, complete launch template reference; the AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup reference shows exactly this pattern (LaunchTemplateId + Version) as the canonical example. The Auto Scaling User Guide (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/launch-templates.html) and the Elastic Beanstalk migration page confirm launch templates are the recommended mechanism and that launch configurations are no longer supported for new accounts as of October 1, 2024. Since the deployed group derives instance configuration solely from a launch template and LaunchConfigurationName is absent (its absence carries no default that would introduce a launch configuration — a group has one instance-configuration source, and here it is the template), the resource ends up in the state the rule demands. No unresolved deployment-time value affects the verdict: even if the launch template ID or version were a parameter, any resolved value still yields a launch-template-based group.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references a launch template directly by launch template name together with a version, and declares no launch configuration
requirements.rationale: The group's instance configuration comes from a launch template — specified by launch template name plus the required version, a valid LaunchTemplateSpecification — and no launch configuration is used, which is exactly the state the rule requires.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation/CDK reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup LaunchTemplateSpecification: it documents that you must specify either LaunchTemplateId or LaunchTemplateName (not both) and that Version is Required: Yes. So "launch template name + version" is a complete, valid launch template reference — the deployed Auto Scaling group will launch instances from that launch template, not from a launch configuration. Also searched the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide, which recommends launch templates over launch configurations (accounts created on or after October 1, 2024 cannot create launch configurations at all), confirming launch-template use is the compliant end state this rule targets. Nothing about using the name form rather than the ID form changes the resulting configuration: both resolve to the same launch template at deployment. No launch configuration is declared and no LaunchConfigurationName is referenced, so there is no absent-value default to consider on the launch configuration side. Verdict: compliant, no finding owed.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group uses a mixed instances policy whose launch template reference identifies a launch template by id and version and declares no per-instance-type overrides, with no direct launch template reference and no launch configuration
requirements.rationale: A mixed instances policy launches instances from the launch template named in its LaunchTemplateSpecification (id plus version) and cannot be backed by a launch configuration, so the group runs entirely on a launch template even with no overrides and no top-level LaunchTemplate property.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether specifying the launch template inside MixedInstancesPolicy.LaunchTemplate.LaunchTemplateSpecification (rather than the ASG's top-level LaunchTemplate property) still means the group uses a launch template. Searched CloudFormation/reference docs for "AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup MixedInstancesPolicy LaunchTemplate LaunchConfigurationName" and for whether Overrides are required. The MixedInstancesPolicy property reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-mixedinstancespolicy.md) states: "You must use a launch template to configure the policy. You cannot use a launch configuration." The ASG LaunchTemplate property docs add that "You can alternatively associate a launch template to the Auto Scaling group by specifying a MixedInstancesPolicy" and that if LaunchTemplate is omitted you must specify MixedInstancesPolicy, LaunchConfigurationName, or InstanceId — so MixedInstancesPolicy is an accepted, equivalent way to attach a launch template. Within MixedInstancesPolicy.LaunchTemplate, only LaunchTemplateSpecification carries the template identity; Overrides merely "override the same properties in the launch template" (Auto Scaling API reference, LaunchTemplate structure) and is optional, so its absence means instances launch exactly as the referenced template version defines. A template id with an explicit version fully resolves the template. No launch configuration is present anywhere in the configuration, and no absent value defaults to one (the service applies no launch-configuration default). The resource therefore ends up in the state the rule requires.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group uses a mixed instances policy that identifies a base launch template and additionally supplies per-instance-type overrides, each override naming its own launch template
requirements.rationale: A mixed instances policy provisions instances exclusively from launch templates — the policy's base LaunchTemplateSpecification plus the optional per-instance-type override templates — so no launch configuration is involved and the group already satisfies the rule.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation/API reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup MixedInstancesPolicy, LaunchTemplate and LaunchTemplateOverrides, plus general docs on launch configurations vs launch templates. The MixedInstancesPolicy LaunchTemplate property type "specif[ies] the launch templates and instance types (overrides) for a mixed instances policy" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-launchtemplate.html). LaunchTemplateOverrides.LaunchTemplateSpecification "[p]rovides a launch template for the specified instance type or set of instance requirements... If not provided, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses the launch template that's specified in the LaunchTemplate definition," and the limit is 20 launch templates counting both overrides and the base definition. So the configuration described — a base launch template with each override naming its own launch template — resolves at runtime to launch templates only, for every instance type the group launches; there is no fallback to, and no ability to reference, a launch configuration inside a mixed instances policy (AWS documents mixed instance policies as a feature that only works with launch templates: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/amazon-ec2-auto-scaling-will-no-longer-add-support-for-new-ec2-features-to-launch-configurations/). Nothing here is deferred to deployment time in a way that could change the answer: whichever template IDs/versions the parameters resolve to, they are still launch templates. The rule's target state — group launches from a launch template, not a LaunchConfigurationName — is therefore met, so the rule owes this configuration no finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group declares no launch source at all: no launch configuration name, no launch template reference, and no mixed instances policy
requirements.rationale: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling supplies no default launch source, so a group that names neither a launch template nor a mixed instances policy will never run on a launch template — the launch-template requirement is unmet regardless of the fact that no launch configuration is named either.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation template reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup and its LaunchTemplate/MixedInstancesPolicy properties, plus the CreateAutoScalingGroup API/SDK references. The LaunchTemplate property documentation states explicitly: "If you omit this property, you must specify MixedInstancesPolicy, LaunchConfigurationName, or InstanceId" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup.html, mirrored at the CDK CfnAutoScalingGroup property docs). Each individual property is "Required: No", but the service applies no default launch source of any kind — there is no implicit launch template, launch configuration, or instance to inherit configuration from. Therefore the configuration described can only resolve one of two ways, and both fail the rule: either the service rejects the group (no launch template in effect), or the launch source is being supplied outside the scanned declaration and cannot be shown to be a launch template. Because no documented default provides a launch template, the state the resource would end up in never satisfies "must use a launch template," so the rule owes a finding. This is not merely an absent-value inference: the cited doc establishes that absence here means no launch source at all, not a safe default.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group is based on the identifier of an existing EC2 instance instead of a launch configuration, launch template, or mixed instances policy
requirements.rationale: Basing an Auto Scaling group on an existing EC2 instance ID makes Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling generate a launch configuration from that instance's settings, so the deployed group runs on a launch configuration rather than a launch template.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on what configuration source the group actually ends up with when only an instance ID is supplied. Searched AWS docs for "CreateAutoScalingGroup InstanceId creates a launch configuration derived from the instance" and "Auto Scaling group from EC2 instance InstanceId launch configuration created for you". The CreateAutoScalingGroup API reference for InstanceId states: "The ID of the instance used to base the launch configuration on. If specified, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses the configuration values from the specified instance to create a new launch configuration." The CloudFormation/CDK CfnAutoScalingGroup docs for the same property likewise describe it as "The ID of the instance used to base the launch configuration on," alongside the statement that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling configures instances using either a launch template or a launch configuration and that launch configurations are strongly discouraged. So the absence of a launch template here is not an unresolved gap: the service resolves the InstanceId into a launch configuration, and the group runs with a launch configuration and no launch template. That is the exact state the rule prohibits, and neither a mixed instances policy nor a launch template is present to satisfy it. The instance ID is a concrete configured value known at analysis time, so no deployment-time-unknown exception applies.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group carries a direct launch template reference that supplies only a version and identifies no launch template by either id or name
requirements.rationale: A LaunchTemplate block that gives only a Version identifies no launch template at all — Auto Scaling requires either LaunchTemplateId or LaunchTemplateName for the reference to resolve, so the group is not actually configured to use a launch template.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether a LaunchTemplate property containing only Version counts as "configured to use a launch template". Searched CloudFormation and Auto Scaling API references for the LaunchTemplateSpecification contract. The CloudFormation property reference (AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup LaunchTemplateSpecification) states up front: "You must specify the following: The ID or the name of the launch template, but not both. The version of the launch template." LaunchTemplateId and LaunchTemplateName are each Required: Conditional with the note "You must specify the LaunchTemplateName or the LaunchTemplateID, but not both"; Version alone is not sufficient. The Auto Scaling API model for LaunchTemplateSpecification repeats the same condition ("Conditional: You must specify either a LaunchTemplateId or a LaunchTemplateName"). Unlike Version — which the API defaults to $Default when omitted — there is no documented default for the identifier: absent an id or name, the service has nothing to resolve and the CreateAutoScalingGroup/stack operation is rejected, so no launch template is ever attached to the group. This is not a deployment-time unknown either; the identifier is absent outright rather than supplied by an unresolved parameter, so every possible outcome leaves the group without a usable launch template reference. The rule's requirement — that the group actually run from a launch template — is therefore unmet, and the rule owes this configuration a finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group uses a mixed instances policy whose launch template reference supplies only a version and identifies no launch template by either id or name
requirements.rationale: A mixed instances policy launch template reference that gives only a version identifies no launch template at all — AWS requires either LaunchTemplateId or LaunchTemplateName, and there is no default that fills one in — so the group does not end up running on a launch template.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether a LaunchTemplateSpecification carrying only Version, nested under MixedInstancesPolicy.LaunchTemplate, results in an Auto Scaling group that actually runs from a launch template. Searched the CloudFormation template reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup LaunchTemplateSpecification and the Security Hub ASFF definition of AwsAutoScalingAutoScalingGroupMixedInstancesPolicyLaunchTemplateLaunchTemplateSpecification. The CFN property type page states outright: "You must specify the following: The ID or the name of the launch template, but not both. The version of the launch template." Both LaunchTemplateId and LaunchTemplateName are documented as "Required: Conditional" with the note "You must specify the LaunchTemplateID or the LaunchTemplateName, but not both"; Version alone is "Required: Yes". Nothing in the documentation describes a default or fallback that resolves a launch template when neither identifier is present — there is no notion of an implicit or inferred template, so the absence here is not an omitted setting with a safe service default but an unidentified resource reference. The resource therefore never reaches the state the rule demands (an ASG provisioning instances from a named launch template); at best the stack fails validation, and in no case is a launch template in effect. Absence of a launch configuration does not rescue it, because the rule requires affirmative use of a launch template, not merely the non-use of a launch configuration. Flag, settled by the CloudFormation property reference.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's launch configuration reference is present but set to an empty string, with no launch template reference and no mixed instances policy
requirements.rationale: The group has no launch template reference and no mixed instances policy launch template, so whatever the empty LaunchConfigurationName value resolves to the group ends up without launch-template-based instance configuration, which is exactly what the rule requires — and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling applies no implicit launch template default.
requirements.evidence:
The verdict turns on whether an Auto Scaling group whose only instance-configuration property is an empty LaunchConfigurationName could still end up backed by a launch template. Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup (LaunchConfigurationName / LaunchTemplate / MixedInstancesPolicy): all three instance-configuration properties are documented as "Required: No" individually, and there is no documented default that supplies a launch template when LaunchTemplate and MixedInstancesPolicy are both omitted — the service never substitutes a launch template for you. Also searched the EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide: "Create a launch configuration" and "Create Auto Scaling groups using launch configurations" state that launch configurations are legacy (no new instance types since January 1, 2023; accounts created on or after October 1, 2024 cannot create them by any method including CloudFormation), and AWS explicitly recommends migrating Auto Scaling groups to launch templates. So the documentation confirms both that launch-configuration-style groups are the state the rule targets and that no default launch template exists.

Here the launch configuration reference is present but empty, and no launch template or mixed instances policy is present. The empty string is not a deployment-time unknown — it is a concrete, readable value — so the intrinsic-exception path does not apply. Either the empty name is rejected/resolves to no valid launch configuration, or it is treated as a launch configuration reference; in every case the resulting group has no launch template, which is the condition the rule flags. Nothing in the configuration can make it compliant, so the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's launch template reference takes its identifying value entirely from an input that is only known at deployment time
requirements.rationale: The group already specifies a LaunchTemplate reference, and the rule turns on which provisioning mechanism the group uses rather than which template it points at, so an unresolved template ID or name still resolves to a launch template and never to a launch configuration.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup's LaunchTemplate / LaunchTemplateSpecification and LaunchConfigurationName, plus the EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide on choosing a launch template versus a launch configuration. The reference for LaunchTemplateSpecification (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-launchtemplatespecification.html) states it "Specifies a launch template to use when provisioning EC2 instances for an Auto Scaling group" and requires "The ID or the name of the launch template, but not both" plus the version — the identifying value selects *which* launch template, not whether a launch template is used. The service's two mutually exclusive options are the LaunchTemplate/MixedInstancesPolicy path and the separate LaunchConfigurationName path (the User Guide "Choose launch template or configuration" page confirms these are the two alternatives, and recommends launch templates; launch configurations are no longer supported for accounts created after October 1, 2024). Therefore, for a group whose LaunchTemplateId/LaunchTemplateName comes from a deployment-time input, the deciding fact for this rule — the presence of a launch template reference instead of a launch configuration — is fully known at analysis time. Every possible value the input can take yields a launch template, so the compliant outcome is certain; this is decided on the merits rather than deferred as an unresolvable intrinsic, and no strict-default tie-break is needed.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's launch configuration name takes its value entirely from an input that is only known at deployment time, with no launch template reference and no mixed instances policy
requirements.rationale: The Auto Scaling group launches instances from a launch configuration no matter what name the deploy-time input resolves to — every possible value yields a launch-configuration-backed group with no launch template — so the rule's condition is breached regardless of the unknown value.
requirements.evidence: What the verdict turns on: whether an unresolvable (deploy-time) value for LaunchConfigurationName makes the configuration unknowable, or whether the launch mechanism is already determined. Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup (LaunchConfigurationName / LaunchTemplate / MixedInstancesPolicy) and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide on launch configurations vs. launch templates. The resource schema treats LaunchConfigurationName, LaunchTemplate, and MixedInstancesPolicy as distinct, mutually exclusive ways to specify the instance configuration; the MixedInstancesPolicy reference states outright "You must use a launch template to configure the policy. You cannot use a launch configuration." The user guide pages (Create a launch configuration; Create Auto Scaling groups using launch configurations) confirm launch configurations are a separate, deprecated mechanism — new instance types unsupported since January 1, 2023, and accounts created on or after October 1, 2024 cannot create them by any method including CloudFormation — and recommend migrating to launch templates. Here the group specifies LaunchConfigurationName with no LaunchTemplate and no MixedInstancesPolicy. The deployment-time input only decides *which* launch configuration is referenced, not *whether* a launch configuration is used; the property being populated at all fixes the mechanism. Since every value the input could take produces a launch-configuration-backed Auto Scaling group, the outcome is known at analysis time and the deploy-time-unknown exception does not apply. There is also no default that could rescue it: omitting a launch template does not cause the service to supply one. Decided on the documented semantics of the properties.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group uses a mixed instances policy that contains no launch template specification at all, with no direct launch template reference and no launch configuration
requirements.rationale: A mixed instances policy with no launch template specification inside it supplies no launch template at all — the service applies no default launch template, so the group has no launch template in effect and fails the requirement.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation/API reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup MixedInstancesPolicy and its LaunchTemplate sub-property. The AutoScalingGroup resource reference states: "LaunchTemplate ... You can alternatively associate a launch template to the Auto Scaling group by specifying a MixedInstancesPolicy. ... If you omit this property, you must specify MixedInstancesPolicy, LaunchConfigurationName, or InstanceId." So a MixedInstancesPolicy is only a valid substitute for a direct LaunchTemplate because the policy itself carries the launch template. The MixedInstancesPolicy property page (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-mixedinstancespolicy.md) documents its LaunchTemplate sub-property as "Required: Yes" and states "You must use a launch template to configure the policy. You cannot use a launch configuration." No default launch template is documented for an omitted MixedInstancesPolicy.LaunchTemplate — the service does not substitute one; the configuration is simply incomplete and provides no launch template reference. Since neither a direct LaunchTemplate, nor a launch template inside the mixed instances policy, nor any other resolvable launch template source is present, the group as described does not use a launch template, so the rule's requirement is unmet. The value is not deployment-time-unknown (nothing is deferred to a parameter), so the intrinsic exception does not apply.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group carries a direct launch template reference whose launch template id is set to an empty string, with no launch configuration
requirements.rationale: An empty launch template id is not a usable launch template reference — the Auto Scaling API requires a LaunchTemplateId of at least 1 character (or a LaunchTemplateName instead), so the group ends up with no valid launch template and therefore does not satisfy the requirement to run from one.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation template reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup LaunchTemplateSpecification and the autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group CLI/API reference. The LaunchTemplateSpecification docs state that you must specify either the LaunchTemplateId or the LaunchTemplateName (but not both) plus a Version; the API reference for the --launch-template structure gives LaunchTemplateId constraints of min 1, max 255 characters, and says "Conditional: You must specify either a LaunchTemplateId or a LaunchTemplateName." An empty string therefore fails the length constraint and identifies no launch template; there is no service default that substitutes a launch template when the id is blank, and no launch configuration is present either, so the group is left with no valid launch-template-based configuration. The value is a literal empty string known at analysis time, not a deployment-time input, so the intrinsic-exception carve-out does not apply. The presence of a LaunchTemplate block alone does not put the resource in the state the rule requires, so the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group uses a mixed instances policy whose launch template identifier takes its value entirely from an input only known at deployment time
requirements.rationale: A mixed instances policy can only reference a launch template — never a launch configuration — so the group provably launches from a launch template even though the template's identifier resolves to a deployment-time input value.
requirements.evidence: The rule turns on whether the Auto Scaling group launches instances from a launch template or from a launch configuration. Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup and its MixedInstancesPolicy property type. The MixedInstancesPolicy page states verbatim: "You must use a launch template to configure the policy. You cannot use a launch configuration." The parent resource page confirms the mutual exclusivity from the other direction: LaunchConfigurationName is "Required only if you don't specify LaunchTemplate, MixedInstancesPolicy, or InstanceId," and LaunchTemplate notes "You can alternatively associate a launch template to the Auto Scaling group by specifying a MixedInstancesPolicy." MixedInstancesPolicy.LaunchTemplate carries a LaunchTemplateSpecification, i.e. a launch template reference by definition. The unknown here is only which launch template is referenced (name/ID supplied by a deployment-time input), not whether a launch template is used. Every possible resolved value of that input still yields a launch-template-backed group, so the rule's compliance condition is satisfied for all resolutions and the deploy-time unknown does not need the intrinsic-value exception — the merits decide it as compliant.
